sections.label: Decision to intervene on rent
sections.summary: The speaker says feedback was monitored and the situation assessed, and a decision was made to intervene more substantively on rent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We have monitored feedback, assessed the situation, thought carefully about what else needed to be done.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And we have decided to intervene in a more substantive way to deal with the issue of rent.

sections.label: MTI contraction forecast
sections.summary: MTI is now forecasting a contraction of between 4% and 7%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: MTI is now forecasting a contraction of between 4% and 7%.

sections.label: April 2020 decline
sections.summary: In April 2020, they declined by 53% on a year-on-year basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In April 2020, they declined by 53% on a year-on-year basis.

sections.label: Manpower support and rental Bill
sections.summary: The Government put in the Jobs Support Scheme, waived the Foreign Worker Levy and other schemes, and this Bill deals with rental obligations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As regards manpower, the Government through the various Budgets has put in the Jobs Support Scheme, waived the Foreign Worker Levy and put in a number of other schemes to help, together with partners like NTUC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to deal with the rental obligations, amongst other things.

sections.label: Chope survey on restaurants
sections.summary: A Chope survey found 81% of respondents said they could not operate beyond six months, based on circuit breaker cost and revenue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If you look at restaurant booking platform Chope, they did a survey: 81% of their respondents said they would not be able to operate beyond the next six months, based on cost and revenue that they had during the circuit breaker period.

sections.label: Four Budgets and rental assistance
sections.summary: Four Budgets amounting to almost $93 billion included two months' rental assistance for retail and F&B tenants and one month for office and industrial tenants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: On the Government’s part, you have seen four Budgets amounting to almost $93 billion, including two months' rental assistance for retail, F&B tenants; one month for office and industrial tenants, as well as broad salary support and other credit-easing facilities.

sections.label: SMEs GDP and employment share
sections.summary: In 2019, Singapore's 260,000 SMEs contributed 45% of GDP and 72% of employment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In 2019, the 260,000 SMEs in Singapore contributed to 45% of our GDP and 72% of our employment.

sections.label: SME eligibility criteria
sections.summary: Eligibility covers SMEs renting commercial, industrial or office space with turnover up to S$100 million and over 35% turnover reduction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: My third and final point is: go back to the eligibility criteria.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: They cover SME renting commercial, industrial or office space for the operation of their business and those with a turnover of not more than S$100 million per annum and where they had a reduction in turnover of more than 35%, which is a substantial hit.

sections.label: Further landlord rent waiver
sections.summary: Landlords may be required to waive up to two further months' rent for qualifying SME tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Second, landlords may also be required to provide a further waiver of up to two months’ of rent to qualifying SME tenants.

sections.label: Government rental assistance amounts
sections.summary: Government provides about two months' rental assistance for eligible SME tenants of qualifying commercial properties and about one month for other non-residential properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Government will be providing approximately two months of rental assistance for eligible SME tenants of qualifying commercial properties and approximately one month of rental assistance for eligible SME tenants of other non-residential properties; basically, industrial and office properties.

sections.label: Landlords matching government waivers
sections.summary: The Bill requires landlords to grant qualifying SME commercial tenants two months' and industrial and office tenants one month's additional base rent waiver, for those with at least 35% revenue drop.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Bill will require landlords to match what the Government is doing.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They will be required to grant qualifying SME commercial tenants an additional waiver of two months’ rental, of base rent; and qualifying SME industrial and office tenants an additional one month’s waiver of base rent.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This additional relief will apply to SME tenants who have suffered at least a 35% drop in average monthly revenue in April and May 2020, compared to the same period in 2019.

sections.label: Deferment of rental arrears
sections.summary: Eligible SME tenants can defer payment of part of rental arrears accrued from 1 February until 19 October 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: SME tenants who are eligible for the additional relief described above can also get relief under the third plank of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They will be allowed to defer payment of a part of the rental arrears accrued from 1 February, until 19 October 2020.

sections.label: Rental arrears instalment repayment
sections.summary: Tenants may repay rental arrears in equal instalments of up to nine months, with interest capped at 3% per annum, and five months' base rent for commercial properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Tenants can elect to repay their rental arrears in equal instalments, with payment of the first instalment to start no later than November 2020 and that can be done during the duration of the remaining term of their tenancy, up to a maximum of nine months, with interest capped at 3% per annum.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For commercial properties, the maximum amount of arrears that can be paid in instalments, will be five months’ base rent.

sections.label: S-REIT leverage limits
sections.summary: Leverage limits for S-REITs have been increased from 45% to 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Leverage limits for S-REITs have also been increased from 45% to 50%.

sections.label: Assessor relief for contracts
sections.summary: The Bill lets parties apply to an Assessor, who may adjust prescribed obligations or vary a prescribed term for a just and equitable outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Bill therefore provides a mechanism for parties in some of these contracts to seek relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They will be allowed to apply to an Assessor, who may then make a determination to either adjust the manner in which prescribed obligations are to be performed; or vary a prescribed term in a contract in order to achieve a just and equitable outcome.

sections.label: Notifications and determination applications
sections.summary: As of 1 June, more than 4,000 Notifications for Relief and about 500 applications for determinations have been filed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As of 1 June, we have had more than 4,000 Notifications for Relief and about 500 applications for determinations have been filed.

sections.label: Cap on late payment interest
sections.summary: For late payment, payment arrears and interests accumulating during the COVID 1 relief period, a cap will be put on late payment interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For late payment, payment arrears and interests that accumulate during the relief period under COVID 1, we will put a cap on how much late payment interest there can be.

sections.label: SMEs benefiting from rental assistance
sections.summary: Up to 260,000 SMEs may benefit from the Government rental assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: All in all, up to 260,000 SMEs may benefit from the Government rental assistance.

sections.label: Lawyers drafting COVID Bill
sections.summary: Three lawyers worked until 5.00 am for two weeks, and the Attorney-General led drafting with a corporate lawyer's help.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The three lawyers: Lee Chuan Huei, Hema Subramanian and Leong Kit Yu who worked until 5.00 am regularly for the entire two weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This legislation could not have been drafted in most places in three weeks, let alone conceptualise, crystallise and draft, led by our Attorney-General, Mr Lucien Wong.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I said some things about him during the Second Reading of COVID 1.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think it helped tremendously that we had one of the best corporate lawyers in the world helping us from day one, word for word, conceptualising it, checking every word.

sections.label: Public Service preparing Bill
sections.summary: The speaker says preparing the Bill showed the best of the Public Service working together for the broader public.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But it gave me a lot of confidence that he was doing that.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, in this Bill, preparing it, we saw the best of the Public Service at work – coming together, working for the benefit of the broader public.

sections.label: Rental waivers for SME tenants
sections.summary: The Bill institutes rental waivers for SMEs co-paid by Government and landlord, with periods and a reported 35% revenue fall criterion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: One of the main thrusts of the Bill is instituting rental waivers for SMEs, co-paid by the Government and the landlord.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The period is four months for SME tenants at commercial properties for the months of April to July and two months for those in industrial and office properties for the months of April to May.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to news reports, one important criterion is that there must be a 35% fall in average monthly revenue from April to May 2020 compared to the same period last year.

sections.label: Flexible definition of financial hardship
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to define financial hardship broadly and flexibly to balance smaller and larger corporate landlords.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But three, we need a flexible system to differentiate between large corporate landlords and the landlords who have invested in small commercial shophouses and spaces as a form of, say, retirement income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is for this reason that I am asking the Minister for "financial hardship" to be defined broadly and flexibly to strike the right balance, between the smaller landlords and the larger corporate landlords.

sections.label: No double rent for holding over
sections.summary: For tenants unable to move out, landlords will not get double rent for the period of holding over.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For tenants who are unable to move out, there is a change to the normal law of tenancy in saying that landlords will not get double rent for the period of holding over.

sections.label: Capping late payment interest
sections.summary: The Bill looks to cap late payment interest and charges for arrears, which the speaker welcomes to reduce snowballing debt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Bill looks to cap late payment interest, charges for arrears and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I welcome the reduction and limitation of late payment interest as this will help reduce snowballing debt.

sections.label: Sanctity of contract and retrospective measures
sections.summary: The passage states that sanctity of contract and avoiding retrospective measures should be aspired to, and that the Bill will reduce business pain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Indeed, sanctity of contract and the avoidance of retrospective measures are what we should all aspire to to ensure the certainty of the bargain struck by two contracting parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill, if passed, will reduce the pain businesses are feeling.

sections.label: April performance drop statistics
sections.summary: Department of Statistics data shows a 40.5% drop in performance in April, the largest since 1986.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The latest Department of Statistics data has also shown that in April there has been a dramatic drop in performance of 40.5% and this is the largest since 1986.

sections.label: Rent waivers for SME tenants
sections.summary: Eligible SME tenants in commercial properties get two months' rent waiver, while industrial and office tenants get one month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For eligible SME tenants in commercial properties, the landlords are required to waive two months of rent and tenants of industrial and office properties will receive one month’s waiver of rent.

sections.label: Eligibility criteria for SME relief
sections.summary: Relief is for SMEs under $100 million turnover facing COVID-19 cashflow difficulties, with a 35% revenue drop and tenancy before March 25.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Eligibility for the relief are for SMEs with less than $100 million turnover that rent premises for their businesses and are facing cashflow difficulties as a result of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, to be eligible, SMEs also have to fulfil two other criteria of a 35% or more drop in average monthly revenue from April to May on a year-on-year basis, and the tenancy must have been entered before March 25 of this year Landlords are also not required to help larger SME tenants who may have better access to financing or tenants who have seen an increase in business during the period such as supermarkets.

sections.label: Minister for Law on rent intervention
sections.summary: The Minister for Law outlined exceptional circumstances warranting intervention in SME rent as an exception to sanctity of contract.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The hon Minister for Law took pains to outline the exceptional circumstances warranting intervention in the area of rent payable by SMEs as an exception against the principle of sanctity of contract.

sections.label: Cash grants to sub-tenants
sections.summary: The Government under this Bill is prepared to pay cash grants to sub-tenants in possession of the properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As I understand, the Government under this Bill is prepared to pay cash grant to sub-tenants if they are in possession of the properties.

sections.label: Prescribed rate and SME beneficiaries
sections.summary: The Minister said the prescribed rate is no more than 3% per annum and potentially 260,000 SMEs may benefit under the amendment Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The hon Minister mentioned that the prescribed rate is no more than 3% per annum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The hon Minister mentioned that potentially 260,000 SMEs may be beneficiaries under this amendment Bill once passed.

sections.label: No cash movement required
sections.summary: The Bill does not require cash to move from the Government to the property owner to the actual tenant or sub-tenant.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Conceptually, how this works is – to answer Mr Pillai's specific question – the Bill does not require cash to move from the Government to the property owner to the actual tenant or sub-tenant.

sections.label: Two months waiver for everyone
sections.summary: Everyone will get two months on this waiver mechanism.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Everyone will get two months on this waiver mechanism.

sections.label: Set-off of direct monetary assistance
sections.summary: Landlords may set off direct monetary assistance already given against the rental waiver they must provide.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Landlords will be allowed to set off any direct monetary assistance that they have already given against the rental waiver that they are required to provide.

sections.label: 3% interest rate rationale
sections.summary: The 3% interest is comparable to the median secured bank loan rate in April 2020 and balances landlords' and tenants' needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The 3% interest is comparable to the median rate of secured bank loans in April 2020 and takes into consideration the landlords' cost of capital with property as security.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We are aware that some landlords' cost of capital could be higher than 3% but this rate is intended to strike a balance between the needs of landlords who have their own financial obligations, and the tenants who do face significant challenges repaying their rental obligations under these fairly extraordinary circumstances.

sections.label: Arrears period for repayment
sections.summary: Only arrears accruing from 1 February 2020 until 19 October 2020 can be repaid under this repayment schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: To be clear as well, only arrears that accrue from 1 February 2020 until 19 October 2020 can be repaid under this repayment schedule.

sections.label: Factors for landlord rental waiver
sections.summary: Two factors are considered for when landlords cannot provide additional rental waiver: property annual value and rental's proportion of total income.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We considered the factors that should be taken into account as to when landlords should considered to be unable to provide the additional rental waiver.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We think that the two factors to be taken into account are the annual value of their properties and the proportion the rental forms of the landlord's total income.

sections.label: Relief for circuit breaker period
sections.summary: Relief ought to be given for the two months when circuit breaker rules told businesses not to operate.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: When we have imposed the circuit breaker rules for two months telling businesses not to operate, then I think we ought to give relief for that period.

sections.label: Rental waiver as lifeline
sections.summary: Viable businesses facing a 60% turnover drop in April will fail, so a few months rental waiver is thrown as a lifeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Even perfectly viable businesses, given the kind of hit that I have pointed out – 60% drop in turnover in April and probably as bad if not more for May – viable businesses will go down, their employees will go down, people will lose a lot of money.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, I would say it is not as if we are asking them to get down to a cruise liner and everyone is going to be saved.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We are throwing them a lifeline of a few months rental waiver.

sections.label: Help for micro and small businesses
sections.summary: Measures are being considered to assess micro and small businesses needing help in winding up or debt restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In addition to the measures already taken under COVID 1, we are also considering measures to assess certain micro and small businesses which may need help in winding up or where appropriate, with debt restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is still work-in-progress and we do it when we can do it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This answers Mr de Souza's question on whether the Government has any plans to make further adjustments to the insolvency framework so that non-viable businesses that need to exit are able to do so smoothly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Today, Sir, after the conclusion of proceedings on the Second Supplementary Supply (FY 2020) Bill.
